In-context learning is a form of meta-learning used within a language model's forward pass during inference time. It involves the use of the text input as a task specification. The model learns from the input and uses its learned abilities to complete tasks within new contexts.

Few-shot learning is a method of language model adaptation where a model learns to perform a new task by being given only a small number of demonstration examples (usually just one).  This contrasts with traditional fine-tuning, which requires a large amount of labeled data for each task.  The benefits of few-shot learning include reduced reliance on task-specific data and quicker adaptation to new tasks, though it can result in slightly lower performance than state-of-the-art fine-tuned models.
